coordinate_system.rect_semantics: approximate crop rectangle around artwork; section headings and captions excluded

analysis.style: full-colour retro sci-fi pixel-art, Mega Drive / Phantasy Star-inspired tactical strategy look
analysis.important_accuracy_note: The source is a generated presentation sheet, not a production-ready pixel atlas. Its elements are not natively 32x32 pixels; the coordinate rectangles below are approximate source-image crops that should be trimmed, background-cleaned, and resampled to 32x32.
analysis.transparency_note: The PNG is RGBA, but the rendered backdrop contains mixed alpha and hazy colour in places. Do not assume every crop has a clean transparent background.
analysis.terrain_note: Terrain entries are visually identified and mapped, but seamless edge matching has not been tested. Forest/jungle/hills/mountains/river/bridge/road/city/barrier/rubble are better treated as feature or connection tiles than simple endlessly repeating textures.
analysis.coordinate_confidence: approximate visual bounding boxes; suitable as a starting manifest, not pixel-perfect auto-slicing metadata

sprites.label: Soldier
sprites.description: Balanced frontline rifle unit with 6 HP, 70 aim, 12-tile mobility and no armour, dealing 2–4 damage with a reliable standard rifle.

sprites.label: Sniper
sprites.description: Long-range specialist with 5 HP, 85 aim, 10-tile mobility and no armour, dealing 4–6 damage with a sniper rifle but gaining a bonus when stationary.

sprites.label: Heavy
sprites.description: Armoured fire-support unit with 8 HP, 65 aim, 9-tile mobility and 2 armour, dealing 3–5 damage with a heavy weapon that can suppress clustered enemies.

sprites.label: Tech
sprites.description: Electronic-warfare specialist with 6 HP, 70 aim, 11-tile mobility and 1 armour, using a pulse weapon for 2–4 damage and hacking robots, turrets and terminals.

sprites.label: Medic
sprites.description: Combat medic with 6 HP, 70 aim, 12-tile mobility and no armour, dealing 2–3 rifle damage and restoring 3 HP to an adjacent ally twice per mission.

sprites.label: Psi
sprites.description: Fragile psionic specialist with 5 HP, 75 aim, 11-tile mobility and no armour, dealing 3–5 energy damage and using a short-range control or panic ability.

sprites.label: Recon
sprites.description: Fast scout with 5 HP, 75 aim, 15-tile mobility and no armour, dealing 2–3 damage with a light weapon and revealing a wider area while moving.

sprites.label: Engineer
sprites.description: Field engineer with 6 HP, 65 aim, 11-tile mobility and 1 armour, dealing 1–3 sidearm damage while placing mines, repairing devices and opening sealed routes.

sprites.label: Sectoid
sprites.description: Light psionic alien with 5 HP, 65 aim, 12-tile mobility and no armour, firing plasma for 2–4 damage and occasionally disrupting a soldier with mind attacks.

sprites.label: Mutant
sprites.description: Heavy close-range brute with 10 HP, 65 aim, 10-tile mobility and 2 armour, dealing 3–5 melee damage and resisting ordinary small-arms fire.

sprites.label: Assault
sprites.description: Aggressive alien infantry with 7 HP, 75 aim, 13-tile mobility and 1 armour, dealing 3–5 damage and favouring flanking advances.

sprites.label: Sniper
sprites.description: Enemy marksman with 5 HP, 85 aim, 9-tile mobility and no armour, dealing 4–6 long-range damage while vulnerable if caught out of position.

sprites.label: Drone
sprites.description: Small flying scout drone with 4 HP, 70 aim, 16-tile aerial mobility and 1 armour, dealing 2–3 shock damage while ignoring ground obstacles.

sprites.label: Mech
sprites.description: Heavy combat mech with 12 HP, 70 aim, 9-tile mobility and 3 armour, dealing 3–6 cannon damage and taking extra damage from EMP effects.

sprites.label: Spitter
sprites.description: Acid-spitting alien with 7 HP, 65 aim, 10-tile mobility and no armour, attacking for 2–4 damage and leaving a hazardous acid patch on the ground.

sprites.label: Psi
sprites.description: Elite psionic enemy with 6 HP, 75 aim, 12-tile mobility and 1 armour, using mind control or panic effects and dealing 2–4 energy damage.

sprites.label: Dropship
sprites.description: Mission transport used to deploy the squad and mark the extraction zone, with no ordinary combat stats and a restricted landing footprint.

sprites.label: Rover
sprites.description: Light ground vehicle with 10 HP, 2 armour and 14-tile mobility, carrying a small squad or supplies and providing 2–4 damage support fire.

sprites.label: VTOL
sprites.description: Fast aerial transport with 8 HP, 1 armour and 18-tile flight range, able to cross blocked ground and deliver troops but not occupy normal cover.

sprites.label: Turret
sprites.description: Deployable stationary defence with 8 HP, 3 armour, 75 aim and an 8-tile range, firing for 3–5 damage but unable to move once placed.

sprites.label: Supply
sprites.description: Supply vehicle or drop point that replenishes ammunition and one-use equipment, has no attack and should be protected as a mission asset.

sprites.label: Radar
sprites.description: Reconnaissance scanner that reveals concealed enemies in a 6-tile radius, has no attack and works best from an elevated or exposed position.

sprites.label: Repair mech
sprites.description: Friendly repair platform with 8 HP, 2 armour and 10-tile mobility, restoring 2 HP to an adjacent mechanical ally once per turn instead of attacking.

sprites.label: Unlabelled support unit
sprites.description: Unidentified compact support machine with a suggested 7 HP, 1 armour and 11-tile mobility, best treated as a configurable escort or utility unit until its role is chosen.

sprites.label: Hover
sprites.description: Amphibious hover vehicle with 9 HP, 1 armour and 16-tile mobility, crossing water and rough ground while providing 2–4 light-weapon damage.

sprites.label: Medkit
sprites.description: Single-use pickup that restores 3 HP to the soldier who collects it, with no cover value and an interaction cost of one action.

sprites.label: Ammo
sprites.description: Resupply container that refills one weapon magazine or a chosen ammunition pool, provides half cover and can be looted once.

sprites.label: Energy
sprites.description: Single-use energy pickup that restores one ability charge or gadget charge, provides no cover and disappears when collected.

sprites.label: Computer
sprites.description: Hackable terminal that can reveal map intel, disable security or complete an objective, and blocks line of sight while intact.

sprites.label: Door
sprites.description: Closed doorway that blocks movement and line of sight until opened or destroyed, with a suggested 8 HP if it is destructible.

sprites.label: Ladder
sprites.description: Traversal link between two elevation levels that costs one movement point to use and does not provide cover.

sprites.label: Crate
sprites.description: Small destructible container with 4 HP that provides half cover and may contain ammunition, supplies or a mission item.

sprites.label: Console
sprites.description: Objective console that a soldier can hack or activate with one action to trigger doors, machinery or mission progression.

sections.label: Terrain tiles
sections.important_note: These are labelled as tileable in the source artwork, but opposite-edge pixel matching has not been verified. River, bridge, road, city, forest, hills and similar feature tiles need dedicated transition/connection variants for robust map generation.

sprites.label: Grass
sprites.description: Walkable base ground with movement cost 1, no inherent cover and no hazard, suitable as the default outdoor map surface.

sprites.label: Forest
sprites.description: Dense wooded feature terrain with movement cost 2, heavy cover and reduced enemy visibility, with trunks treated as separate solid blockers.

sprites.label: Jungle
sprites.description: Thick vegetation with movement cost 2, heavy concealment and strong cover, but reduced sight lines and difficult traversal.

sprites.label: Hills
sprites.description: Sloped elevated ground with movement cost 2, a height advantage for aim and vision, and optional low cover on marked rocky cells.

sprites.label: Mountains
sprites.description: Steep high ground that blocks movement and long sight lines unless a pass is added, creating a natural boundary and elevation landmark.

sprites.label: Water
sprites.description: Deep water that is impassable to ordinary infantry, offers no cover and can be crossed only by bridges, aquatic units or special abilities.

sprites.label: River
sprites.description: Watercourse feature that is impassable except at fords or bridges, separates firing lanes and follows connected river-edge variants.

sprites.label: Bridge
sprites.description: Walkable crossing over water with movement cost 1, no inherent cover and a narrow approach that can become a tactical choke point.

sprites.label: Road
sprites.description: Walkable route with movement cost 1 and no cover, suitable for connecting locations and granting a small movement bonus if road rules are enabled.

sprites.label: City
sprites.description: Urban feature zone containing buildings and hard corners, with high cover and blocked sight lines supplied by separate building and wall objects.

sprites.label: Plain
sprites.description: Open walkable base ground with movement cost 1, no cover and clear line of sight, leaving soldiers exposed to enemy fire.

sprites.label: Desert
sprites.description: Dry open base ground with movement cost 1, no cover and no default hazard, making exposed crossings dangerous.

sprites.label: Rock
sprites.description: Rocky base ground with movement cost 1 and no inherent cover, while individual boulders should be placed as separate blocking objects.

sprites.label: Lava
sprites.description: Hazardous ground that ordinary infantry cannot safely cross and that deals 3 damage at the end of each turn to units with heat protection disabled.

sprites.label: Snow
sprites.description: Snow-covered ground with movement cost 2, no inherent cover and clear visibility, slowing advances across open areas.

sprites.label: Swamp
sprites.description: Wet ground with movement cost 2, low visibility and no inherent cover, slowing units and making flanking routes harder to use.

sprites.label: Sand dunes
sprites.description: Loose sand base ground with movement cost 2 and no cover, making long exposed manoeuvres slower than movement across roads or grass.

sprites.label: Crater
sprites.description: Depression feature that remains walkable at movement cost 1 and grants half cover to units occupying its marked low cells.

sprites.label: Tundra
sprites.description: Cold open ground with movement cost 2, no cover and no default damage, creating a slower exposed approach across frozen terrain.

sprites.label: Ice
sprites.description: Slippery walkable ground with movement cost 1 but reduced stopping control, allowing a unit to slide one extra tile if it moves at full speed.

sprites.label: Barrier
sprites.description: Blocking defensive feature with heavy cover on adjacent cells, impassable until breached and destructible with a suggested 10 HP.

sprites.label: Rubble
sprites.description: Broken urban ground with movement cost 2, scattered half-cover positions and obstructed movement, while large debris should be separate objects.

render_hint.placement: separate object layer, not ground tile

sprites.label: Tree
sprites.description: Tall destructible obstacle with 6 HP that blocks movement and line of sight while providing heavy cover to units sheltering beside its trunk.

sprites.label: Bush
sprites.description: Low vegetation with 3 HP that provides half cover and concealment but does not fully block movement or line of sight.

sprites.label: Cactus
sprites.description: Desert obstacle with 4 HP that provides half cover and inflicts 1 contact damage when a unit moves through its occupied tile.

sprites.label: Rocks
sprites.description: Boulder cluster with 8 HP that blocks movement and line of sight and provides heavy cover from adjacent firing positions.

sprites.label: Fence
sprites.description: Low destructible barrier with 4 HP that provides half cover, blocks direct movement and can be vaulted by spending 2 movement points.

sprites.label: Wall
sprites.description: Solid destructible wall with 10 HP that blocks movement and line of sight and provides full cover to soldiers positioned behind it.

sprites.label: Crates
sprites.description: Stacked supply crates with 6 HP that block movement, provide heavy cover and may be searched for a small resource reward.

sprites.label: Barrel
sprites.description: Explosive barrel with 5 HP that detonates when destroyed, dealing 3–5 damage to units within a 1-tile radius.

sprites.label: Fuel tank
sprites.description: Volatile fuel tank with 7 HP that explodes when destroyed, dealing 4–6 damage within a 2-tile radius and possibly igniting nearby ground.

sprites.label: Radio tower
sprites.description: Tall mission landmark that blocks some sight lines and can be captured or hacked to reveal enemy positions across the map.

sprites.label: Satellite dish
sprites.description: Interactable communications objective that can scan a distant sector or disrupt enemy communications after a one-action activation.

sprites.label: Light post
sprites.description: Small destructible light source with 2 HP that illuminates nearby tiles in night missions and provides only minimal physical obstruction.

sprites.label: Power pylon
sprites.description: Energy structure that can power nearby devices or serve as a sabotage objective, provides half cover and may overload when destroyed.

sprites.label: Alien relic
sprites.description: Alien artefact that acts as a high-value objective or research pickup, grants a mission reward when secured and may trigger an enemy response.

sprites.label: UFO wreck
sprites.description: Large crashed craft wreckage that blocks movement and sight lines, provides heavy cover and can be searched for salvage or mission evidence.

sprites.label: Biohazard
sprites.description: Toxic growth or spill that marks a hazardous zone, dealing 1 damage per turn to unprotected units and discouraging occupation.

sprites.label: Move
sprites.description: Movement indicator showing reachable destination tiles for the selected unit, with legal range determined by remaining movement points.

sprites.label: Attack
sprites.description: Attack marker identifying a valid hostile target, with hit chance and damage preview supplied by the combat interface.

sprites.label: Cover
sprites.description: Cover indicator showing a protected position, with half-cover or full-cover strength determined by the tile or adjacent obstacle.

sprites.label: Alert
sprites.description: Warning marker for detected danger or an active threat, prompting the player to check line of sight and enemy intent.

sprites.label: Health
sprites.description: Health indicator representing current and maximum hit points, with low health signalling that the unit may be downed by another hit.

sprites.label: Ammo
sprites.description: Ammunition indicator showing remaining shots in the equipped weapon, with reloads consuming an action when the magazine is empty.

sprites.label: Objective
sprites.description: Mission objective marker identifying an item, area or target that must be secured, activated, defended or destroyed.

sprites.label: Turn
sprites.description: Turn-state marker showing the active player or enemy phase, with actions refreshed when control passes to that side.

sprites.label: Spawn
sprites.description: Deployment marker identifying a valid unit spawn point, with placement restricted by mission rules and occupied tiles.

sprites.label: Target
sprites.description: Target reticle marking the tile or unit currently selected for an attack, ability or interaction.

sprites.label: In range
sprites.description: Range marker indicating that a target is reachable by the selected weapon or ability from the current position.

sprites.label: Blocked
sprites.description: Blocked-action marker showing that line of sight, range, terrain or another rule prevents the selected action.

sprites.label: Vision
sprites.description: Visibility marker showing tiles currently revealed to the squad, with fog of war hiding enemies outside the visible area.

sprites.label: Damage
sprites.description: Damage marker used for floating combat feedback, displaying hit values or critical-hit effects after an attack resolves.

sprites.label: Space cat
sprites.description: Friendly mascot or neutral mission NPC with no combat stats by default, available for rescue, protection or purely decorative appearances.

sprites.label: Penguin
sprites.description: Small neutral wildlife character with no combat stats by default, useful as an oddball map inhabitant or optional rescue target.

sprites.label: Robot chicken
sprites.description: Comic little mechanical companion with no default attack, but it can be assigned a cosmetic follower or a one-off objective role.

sprites.label: Snail
sprites.description: Harmless alien snail with no combat stats by default, suitable as ambient decoration or a slow-moving neutral creature in special missions.

sprites.label: UFO
sprites.description: Small unidentified craft that can serve as a mission objective, extraction prop or scenery, with flight and combat behaviour disabled unless configured.

sprites.label: Flag
sprites.description: Faction or mission flag that marks a control point, ownership state or extraction location and has no combat stats of its own.

ui_markers/alert.label: Alert
ui_markers/alert.description: Warning marker for detected danger or an active threat, prompting the player to check line of sight and enemy intent.

ui_markers/health.label: Health
ui_markers/health.description: Health indicator representing current and maximum hit points, with low health signalling that the unit may be downed by another hit.

ui_markers/ammo.label: Ammo
ui_markers/ammo.description: Ammunition indicator showing remaining shots in the equipped weapon, with reloads consuming an action when the magazine is empty.

ui_markers/objective.label: Objective
ui_markers/objective.description: Mission objective marker identifying an item, area or target that must be secured, activated, defended or destroyed.

ui_markers/turn.label: Turn
ui_markers/turn.description: Turn-state marker showing the active player or enemy phase, with actions refreshed when control passes to that side.

ui_markers/spawn.label: Spawn
ui_markers/spawn.description: Deployment marker identifying a valid unit spawn point, with placement restricted by mission rules and occupied tiles.

ui_markers/target.label: Target
ui_markers/target.description: Target reticle marking the tile or unit currently selected for an attack, ability or interaction.

ui_markers/in_range.label: In range
ui_markers/in_range.description: Range marker indicating that a target is reachable by the selected weapon or ability from the current position.

ui_markers/blocked.label: Blocked
ui_markers/blocked.description: Blocked-action marker showing that line of sight, range, terrain or another rule prevents the selected action.

ui_markers/vision.label: Vision
ui_markers/vision.description: Visibility marker showing tiles currently revealed to the squad, with fog of war hiding enemies outside the visible area.

ui_markers/damage.label: Damage
ui_markers/damage.description: Damage marker used for floating combat feedback, displaying hit values or critical-hit effects after an attack resolves.

quirky_extras/space_cat.label: Space cat
quirky_extras/space_cat.description: Friendly mascot or neutral mission NPC with no combat stats by default, available for rescue, protection or purely decorative appearances.

quirky_extras/penguin.label: Penguin
quirky_extras/penguin.description: Small neutral wildlife character with no combat stats by default, useful as an oddball map inhabitant or optional rescue target.

quirky_extras/robot_chicken.label: Robot chicken
quirky_extras/robot_chicken.description: Comic little mechanical companion with no default attack, but it can be assigned a cosmetic follower or a one-off objective role.

quirky_extras/snail.label: Snail
quirky_extras/snail.description: Harmless alien snail with no combat stats by default, suitable as ambient decoration or a slow-moving neutral creature in special missions.

quirky_extras/ufo.label: UFO
quirky_extras/ufo.description: Small unidentified craft that can serve as a mission objective, extraction prop or scenery, with flight and combat behaviour disabled unless configured.

quirky_extras/flag.label: Flag
quirky_extras/flag.description: Faction or mission flag that marks a control point, ownership state or extraction location and has no combat stats of its own.

description_note: Each sprite has a single-sentence tactical description. Numerical combat values are suggested starting-balance values, not extracted facts from the artwork; tune them during playtesting. Movement is measured in grid tiles per turn, HP is hit points, aim is a percentage-style base hit rating, and armour reduces incoming damage.

gameplay_attribute_conventions.hp: Hit points; a unit is incapacitated at 0 HP.
gameplay_attribute_conventions.aim: Suggested base aim rating on a 0–100 scale before cover, range and status modifiers.
gameplay_attribute_conventions.mobility: Suggested maximum grid tiles moved per turn before action-point or dash rules.
gameplay_attribute_conventions.armour: Suggested flat damage reduction per hit.
gameplay_attribute_conventions.damage: Suggested damage range per successful attack.
gameplay_attribute_conventions.terrain_and_props: Movement, cover, line-of-sight, hazard and interaction effects are proposed defaults and can be changed in the game rules.
